cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD. Moses says, "This is what the LORD has commanded…" (Numbers 30:1). Moses, Israel's leader, is the one talking, but he's passing along someone else's words. He's the delivery guy here, friends, and I respect a good delivery guy.

The answer is that he must do everything he has promised. The command says "…he must not break his word; he must do everything he has promised." (Numbers 30:2). A vow to the LORD is a serious thing, friends. I once told myself I'd dust the whole bakery by Friday, and my dusting record is NOT a good example here.

The answer is True. The text says that when her father "…says nothing to her, then all the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand." (Numbers 30:4). Silence counts for something here, friends. It's like your boss saying, "If I don't hear any objections by noon, we're going with the plan." Noon comes, nobody says a word, and the plan is on.

The answer is that the LORD will absolve her. The command says, "The LORD will absolve her because her father has prohibited her." (Numbers 30:5). The vows don't stand in that case. Notice the timing, too, friends. It's on the day he hears about it.

The answer is False. The text says, "Every vow a widow or divorced woman pledges to fulfill is binding on her." (Numbers 30:9). There's no confirmation step from anyone else, friends. When she makes the vow, it binds her.

The answer is "confirms." The text says, "…if her husband says nothing to her from day to day, then he confirms all the vows and pledges that bind her." (Numbers 30:14). It adds that he confirmed them "…because he said nothing to her on the day he heard about them." Saying nothing turns out to say a lot, friends.

The answer is that he will bear her iniquity. The command says, "But if he nullifies them after he hears of them, then he will bear her iniquity." (Numbers 30:15). That's different from nullifying on the day he hears of them (Numbers 30:12). The text doesn't say more about it, friends, so I won't either.
